issues.legal_issue: A writ cannot be granted solely because another person received similar relief unless the other person’s order was lawful and the claimant’s case was materially similar.
material_facts: The High Court directed restoration of a plot based on restoration granted to another allottee after a settlement before a Lok Adalat.
The High Court did not investigate the facts of the other allottee’s case or find that the restoration order was lawful and justified.
The Administration pointed out that the other allottee had not received a refund of the amount paid, unlike the claimants, but the High Court did not resolve that distinction.
issues.conclusion: The High Court could not grant relief on the basis of discrimination without finding that the comparator’s order was lawful and that the cases were similar in material respects.
issues.legal_principle: The discretionary writ jurisdiction cannot compel an authority to repeat an illegal or unwarranted order. An order or action of an authority does not become a judicial precedent merely because it was made in another case. The claimant’s entitlement must be assessed on the facts and law applicable to that claimant. No statutory provision or earlier case is relied on for this principle.

rule.if: writ_petition_claims_equal_treatment and relief_was_granted_to_comparator and (comparator_order_lawfulness_not_established or material_similarity_not_established)

predicates.writ_petition_claims_equal_treatment: A person seeks relief in a writ petition on the ground that another person received equal treatment.
predicates.relief_was_granted_to_comparator: An authority granted the assertedly comparable person the relief sought by the writ petitioner.
predicates.comparator_order_lawfulness_not_establis: The court has not established that the order granting relief to the comparable person was lawful and justified.
predicates.material_similarity_not_established: The court has not established that the claimant’s case is similar to the comparable person’s case in material respects.

issues.definition: When a writ petitioner relies on another person’s relief but the lawfulness of that relief or material similarity between the cases has not been established, the petitioner cannot obtain relief solely on that basis.

issues.legal_issue: A defaulting allottee who accepted a refund, failed to comply with a later conditional opportunity for restoration, and had already failed in a restoration proceeding could not obtain restoration through a further writ petition on the asserted basis of another allottee’s treatment.
material_facts: The allottees defaulted on an instalment, and their lease was cancelled after notice and an opportunity to be heard.
After the forfeiture was reduced, the allottees took back the balance of their deposit.
A later administrative order offered restoration if the allottees paid the full amount within a specified time, but they did not comply.
A prior writ petition seeking restoration was dismissed, and a review of that dismissal was also rejected.

The later writ petition was allowed by the High Court on the basis of restoration granted to another allottee, without establishing that the cases were materially similar or that the other restoration order was lawful.
issues.conclusion: The appeal was allowed and the High Court’s order was set aside; the allottees were not entitled to restoration on the basis relied on by the High Court.
issues.legal_principle: A writ claim must be decided on its own facts and applicable legal principles; the discretionary writ jurisdiction cannot require an authority to repeat an illegal or unwarranted action. The decision also notes that an earlier restoration opportunity was not taken and that a prior writ seeking restoration had been dismissed. No statutory provision or earlier case is relied on to determine this claim.

rule.if: writ_petition_seeks_plot_restoration and lease_cancelled_after_payment_default and allottee_accepted_refund and conditional_restoration_offer_not_met and prior_restoration_writ_dismissed

predicates.writ_petition_seeks_plot_restoration: An allottee seeks restoration of a plot through a writ petition.
predicates.lease_cancelled_after_payment_default: The allottee’s lease was cancelled after the allottee defaulted on a required payment.
predicates.allottee_accepted_refund: The allottee took back the deposited amount after deduction of the amount forfeited.
predicates.conditional_restoration_offer_not_met: The allottee did not satisfy the payment condition attached to a later opportunity to restore the plot.
predicates.prior_restoration_writ_dismissed: A prior writ petition by the allottee seeking restoration was dismissed.

issues.definition: When an allottee seeks restoration by writ after defaulting, accepting a refund, failing to meet a later restoration condition, and losing an earlier restoration writ, the later restoration claim is denied.

issues.legal_issue: A writ challenging cancellation of a lease was not governed by an earlier decision involving materially different facts where the claimant had accepted the refund and waited seventeen years to challenge the cancellation without substantiating an explanation for the delay.
material_facts: The allottee defaulted on an instalment, and the lease was cancelled after a show-cause process.
In the appeal from cancellation, the allottee sought only a reduction in the forfeiture and did not challenge the cancellation.
After the forfeiture was reduced, the allottee took back the balance of the deposit and remained inactive for seventeen years before challenging the cancellation by writ.
The allottee’s explanation that a revision had been filed and remained pending was not substantiated; the allottee also did not explain the failure to inquire or seek a decision during that period.
The High Court allowed the writ petition on the basis of an earlier decision that concerned materially different facts and grounds.
issues.conclusion: The High Court erred in allowing the writ petition; the appeal was allowed and its judgment set aside.
issues.legal_principle: The earlier decision in Jaswant Singh v. Chandigarh Administration did not govern because its facts and grounds were materially different. The Court expressed no opinion on whether that earlier decision was correct. The claimant’s own conduct and circumstances had to be considered; no statutory provision is cited.

predicates.writ_petition_challenges_lease_cancellat: An allottee brings a writ petition challenging cancellation of a lease.
predicates.allottee_accepted_refund_without_challen: The allottee sought only a reduction in forfeiture, accepted the remaining refund, and did not challenge cancellation at that time.
predicates.challenge_delayed_for_long_period_withou: The allottee waited a long period before challenging cancellation and did not substantiate an explanation for the delay.
predicates.cited_precedent_materially_different: The earlier decision invoked to support the writ petition concerned materially different facts or grounds.

issues.definition: When an allottee accepts a refund without challenging cancellation, later challenges it after a long unexplained period, and relies on a materially different precedent, the writ challenge is denied.
